'''''Chimonanthus praecox''''', also known as '''wintersweet'''<ref name="POWO_139248-1"/> and '''Japanese allspice''',<ref name=GRIN/> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[genus]] ''[[Chimonanthus]]'' of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Calycanthaceae]]. The plant is [[native plant|native]] to China and is known as ''làméi'' ({{linktext|蠟梅}}) in [[Standard Chinese|Chinese]]. It is also grown in Iran, where it is called ''gol-e yakh'' ({{linktext|گل‌یخ}}) or "ice flower" in [[Persian language|Persian]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-07-01 |title=راهنمای نگهداری و پرورش گل و گیاهان زینتی - گل یخ |url=https://nargil.ir/Plant.aspx?Name=Chimonanthus-Praecox&cid=5613 |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=نارگیل}}</ref>

The plant is a vigorous [[deciduous]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|4|m|0|abbr=on}} tall with an erect trunk and leaves {{convert|5|-|29|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2|-|12|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad. Its strongly scented pendent flowers, produced in winter (between November and March in UK,<ref name=oxford>{{cite book |last1=Nicholson |first1=B.E. |last2=Wallis |first2=Michael |year=1963 |title=The Oxford Book of Garden Flowers |location=London |publisher=Oxford University Press |page=viii |isbn=978-0199100026}}</ref>) on bare stems, have 15-21 yellow or pale green-yellow [[tepals]], the inner ones usually with purplish red pigments.<ref>{{cite web|title=eFloras - Flora of China - ''Chimonanthus praecox''|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200008496 | website=Efloras.org|access-date=5 July 2013}}</ref><ref name="GRIN">{{GRIN | access-date = 2008-06-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

This plant is cultivated in gardens, producing valued flower colour during dormant seasons. The [[cultivar]]s ''C. praecox'' 'Grandiflorus'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Chimonanthus praecox'' 'Grandiflorus'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/97272/Chimonanthus-praecox-Grandiflorus/Details | access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> and ''C. praecox'' 'Luteus'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Chimonanthus praecox'' 'Luteus'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/98024/Chimonanthus-praecox-Luteus/Details | access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].

The plant is not closely related to [[allspice]], ''Pimenta dioica''.

==Cultural use==
''C. praecox'' is a common motif in traditional Persian poetry, literature, and music. A more modern example of ''C. praecox'' in Persian music is [[Kourosh Yaghmaei]]'s ''[[Gol-e Yakh]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ati |date=2022-10-20 |title=دانلود آهنگ گل یخ کوروش یغمایی {{!}} با دو کیفیت 320 و 128 {{!}} با متن • موزیکفا |url=https://music-fa.com/download-song/5359/ |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=موزیکفا |language=fa-IR}}</ref>
